paragraphs.title: The Sins of Jerusalem and Its Leaders

answers: As a filthy, polluted, and oppressing city
As a peaceful and joyful city
As a newly built city
easy.explanation: Jerusalem is called “filthy and polluted” and “the oppressing city.”
easy.q: How is Jerusalem described at the beginning of the passage?

answers: In her princes
In the LORD
In the nations
easy.explanation: The verse says, “she trusted not in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom did Jerusalem not trust?

answers: Shepherds
Faithful servants
Evening wolves
easy.explanation: The judges are described as “evening wolves.”
easy.q: What are the judges compared to?

answers: They had kept the law perfectly
They had polluted the sanctuary and done violence to the law
They had gathered the exiles
medium.explanation: The priests had polluted the sanctuary and done violence to the law.
medium.q: What had the priests done according to the passage?

answers: Careless or reckless
Wise and discerning
Humble and obedient
medium.explanation: The prophets are called “light and treacherous persons,” meaning careless and unreliable.
medium.q: What does “light” mean in the description of the prophets?

answers: The city is quiet while the nations are loud
The just LORD is in the midst of the city even though its leaders are sinful
The priests are righteous while the people are sinful
medium.explanation: The LORD is just and present among the people despite the surrounding injustice.

answers: The LORD brings judgment to light continually and reliably
Judgment is given only at night
Judgment is carried out by the city judges
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the regularity and certainty of the LORD’s judgment.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the phrase “every morning”?

answers: They lived in a distant city
They held positions that should have involved righteous leadership
They did not know where Jerusalem was
challenge.explanation: Princes, judges, prophets, and priests failed in the responsibilities of their offices.
challenge.q: Why is the sin of the leaders especially serious?

answers: Jerusalem is exempt from judgment
The city no longer needs leaders
God’s presence does not hide or excuse the city’s injustice
challenge.explanation: Although the LORD is present, the city’s wickedness is still exposed and judged.
challenge.q: What does the LORD’s presence “in the midst thereof” show?

paragraphs.title: Punishment That Did Not Lead to Repentance

answers: He destroyed them and left them desolate
He made them wealthy
He brought them back to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD cut off the nations and made their cities desolate.
easy.q: What did the LORD do to the nations and their cities?

answers: How to build new cities
To fear Him and receive instruction
How to rule the nations
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive instruction.”
easy.q: What did the LORD hope Jerusalem would learn?

answers: She rose early and corrupted all her doings
She repented immediately
She gathered the exiles
easy.explanation: The people “rose early, and corrupted all their doings.”
easy.q: What did Jerusalem do despite the warning?

answers: They were filled with people
They were destroyed and left without inhabitants
They were rebuilt quickly
medium.explanation: Their streets were waste, and there was no man or inhabitant in them.
medium.q: What does the description of the nations’ cities emphasize?

answers: So Jerusalem would learn to fear Him and receive instruction
To praise the kings of those nations
To announce that the cities would be rebuilt
medium.explanation: The destruction was intended as a warning and correction for Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why did the LORD mention the destruction of the nations?

answers: Jerusalem’s continued corruption
The nations bringing offerings
The joy of Zion
medium.explanation: Because the people continued to corrupt their deeds, the LORD announced judgment.
medium.q: What leads to the day of judgment in this passage?

answers: The punishment was not severe enough
The people saw the warning but did not learn from it
The nations were never gathered for judgment
challenge.explanation: The LORD expected Jerusalem to receive instruction, but she continued in corruption.
challenge.q: What is the central failure described in verses 6–7?

answers: It moves from warning Jerusalem to announcing judgment on the nations
It moves from salvation to celebration
It moves from priests to judges
challenge.explanation: After Jerusalem refuses correction, the LORD describes gathering the nations for judgment.
challenge.q: How does the focus change from verse 7 to verse 8?

answers: A limited and mild judgment
The full intensity of divine anger and judgment
Joy over the return of the exiles
challenge.explanation: The phrase highlights the complete force of the LORD’s coming judgment.
challenge.q: What does “all my fierce anger” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Purification of the Nations and the Remnant of Israel

answers: A pure language
Desolate cities
New kings
easy.explanation: The LORD will turn to the peoples “a pure language.”
easy.q: What will the LORD give the peoples after their purification?

answers: To rule Jerusalem
To serve Him with one consent
To avoid bringing offerings
easy.explanation: They will call upon the LORD and serve Him together.
easy.q: Why will the peoples call upon the name of the LORD?

answers: An afflicted and poor people
The proud only
The corrupt priests
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people.”
easy.q: Who will remain in the midst of Jerusalem?

answers: With unity and agreement
In secret
By one person alone
medium.explanation: The peoples will serve the LORD together and in unity.
medium.q: What does “with one consent” mean in this context?

answers: It will increase
It will be removed
It will be transferred to the nations
medium.explanation: The LORD will remove those who rejoice in pride, and Jerusalem will no longer be haughty.
medium.q: What will happen to pride in Jerusalem?

answers: As people who do iniquity and speak lies
As people who trust in the LORD and live without deceit
As people who are always afraid
medium.explanation: The remnant will not do iniquity or speak lies, and it will trust in the LORD.
medium.q: How is the remnant of Israel described?

answers: Both descriptions involve turning to the LORD and living rightly
Both descriptions focus only on destruction
The two descriptions have no connection
challenge.explanation: The nations will serve the LORD together, while the remnant will trust Him and live without deceit.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the purification of the nations and the remnant of Israel?

answers: A change from wrongdoing and lies to righteousness and peace
A change from humility to pride
A change from peace to warfare
challenge.explanation: The remnant will not do iniquity or speak lies, and none will make them afraid.
challenge.q: What moral change is emphasized in the remnant of Israel?

answers: It shows that people from faraway places will also worship the LORD
It shows that only Jerusalem will worship the LORD
It describes the destruction of every nation
challenge.explanation: People from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia will bring an offering to the LORD.
challenge.q: Why is the mention of distant lands important?

paragraphs.title: Zion’s Joy, Salvation, and the Return of the Exiles

answers: The daughter of Zion and Israel
The city judges
The cities of the nations
easy.explanation: The daughter of Zion, Israel, and Jerusalem are called to rejoice.
easy.q: Who is commanded to sing and rejoice?

answers: Her judgments and her enemy
Her joy
Her inhabitants
easy.explanation: The LORD has taken away her judgments and cast out her enemy.
easy.q: What has the LORD removed from Jerusalem?

answers: Those who halt and those who were driven out
The corrupt judges and priests
The ruined cities
easy.explanation: The LORD will save her that halteth and gather her that was driven out.
easy.q: Whom will the LORD gather and save?

answers: People who are joyful
People who are grieving or sorrowful
People who are proud
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to those who are sorrowful and burdened by reproach.
medium.q: What does “sorrowful for the solemn assembly” describe?

answers: Because the LORD is in her midst, has removed her enemies, and will save her
Because she has become deserted
Because the nations have stopped serving the LORD
medium.explanation: The LORD is in her midst as King and mighty Savior.
medium.q: Why is Jerusalem commanded to rejoice?

answers: He will turn their shame into praise and restore them
He will leave them in disgrace
He will send them to the ruined cities
medium.explanation: The LORD will give them praise and fame and turn back their captivity.
medium.q: What will the LORD do for the gathered people and exiles?

answers: His presence is the source of security and salvation
His presence causes Zion to withdraw
His presence prevents all joy
challenge.explanation: The LORD is mighty in Zion and will save, so the people need not fear.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s presence in Zion and the command not to fear?

answers: They move from shame and rejection to praise and honor
They move from honor to shame
They move from wealth to destruction
challenge.explanation: The LORD gathers them and gives them praise and fame where they had been shamed.
challenge.q: What change comes to the outcast and exiles?

answers: The restoration will be visible and openly witnessed
The return will happen secretly
Only the nations will see the return
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to restore the exiles in a way that will be seen by the people.
challenge.q: What does “before your eyes” emphasize at the end of the passage?
